## Description {#details}



This library implements several <b>doubly linked lists</b>, used by some of the <b>µOS++</b> components to manage internal objects. However, its design is sufficiently <b>generic</b> to be valuable in other applications, warranting its packaging as a standalone library.

A key differentiator from <code>std::list</code> is that this implementation <b>does not require dynamic memory allocation</b> for list links, thereby eliminating the need for an allocator. Instead, it employs <b>intrusive lists</b>, where links are stored directly within the list elements.

Another notable feature is <b>statically initialised lists</b>, created in the <b>global scope</b> without modifying their members in constructors. Instead, they are fully <b>initialised</b> by setting their entire content to zero during startup (via <b>BSS initialisation</b>).

This approach enables <b>static objects</b> to <b>auto-register</b> with static registrar instances. As static constructor execution order is undefined, the only reliable way to ensure the registrar is ready before clients attempt to register is to initialise it during <b>startup</b> (via BSS initialisation) prior to the execution of static constructors.
